h1:
Sisaket Mookata & Thai BBQ
10 Value Dinner Spots
intro: Once the sun drops in Sisaket, the dinner locals meet up for most often is mookata and Thai BBQ — gathered around the grill, dipping into spicy jaew sauce, talking until the place closes. We've picked 10 spots that Sisaket folks actually eat at, from pay-by-weight all-you-can-eat buffets to Korean grills in town, with rough prices and neighborhoods so you can match your budget.

blocks.html: Mookata in Sisaket comes in two main styles. The first is the sit-at-the-grill all-you-can-eat buffet — some places charge per person, others charge by weight, where you pay for the weight of the ingredients you take. It's easy on the budget and great for groups. The other style is Korean BBQ, which leans on marinated meats and a wider spread of dishes; prices run higher, but you get the atmosphere for a long, slow meal. A few of these spots sit right in the center of town, an easy walk from the Rajabhat student dorms.

items.name: Piyada Shabu & Mookata
items.blurb: The buffet spot Sisaket locals mention most. It charges by weight based on the ingredients you take, not per head — all-you-can-eat with no time limit. There's pork neck, pork belly, and shabu items to choose from. The shop's page has tens of thousands of followers and several branches around town. It's the first pick for anyone who wants to control their budget and only pay for what they actually eat.
items.meta: Several branches in town (Phon Kha, Pho) · pay-by-weight · no time limit

items.name: Nabhee Grill (Na Mee BBQ Buffet)
items.blurb: A per-person BBQ buffet that's popular in review groups, running around 289 baht for everything included. Reviewers praise the dipping sauce and the variety of ingredients, with both mookata and shabu options. It suits anyone who wants a single flat price with no surprises when the scale comes out.
items.meta: In Sisaket town · per-person buffet · everything included

items.name: Si Thong Mookata & Camping
items.blurb: A seafood-leaning mookata with a camping theme and a relaxed open-air setting that's nice in the evening. It charges by weight at around 279 baht per kilo, with seafood to grill on top of the usual pork. Good for groups that want both the atmosphere and a varied spread.
items.meta: In Sisaket town · camping theme · seafood

items.name: Gluay Gluay Ko Khun Buffet
items.blurb: A BBQ buffet that stands out for its grain-fed (ko khun) beef, with no time limit. Reviewers say the spread really is generous — a friend who went said they were stuffed. People tend to go around 5pm to grab a table before it fills up. It's in the Nong Pho community area, near Rueang Sin Thai rice mill.
items.meta: Soi Eua Arthon village, Nong Pho community · no time limit

items.name: Green Garden
items.blurb: A Korean-style BBQ–shabu buffet in town. The thing people talk about is the refillable pickled seafood, included in the per-person price. It's near Sisaket Rajabhat University and isn't too crowded on weekdays, so it works well for couples or small groups who want to sit and relax.
items.meta: Near Sisaket Rajabhat · per-person buffet · pickled seafood

items.name: Suk Lon Mookata
items.blurb: A small mookata spot on Si Sumang Road run by people who genuinely love eating mookata themselves. Reviewers praise the flavor and the owner's attention to detail. What folks like is that you can bring your dog — good for a chill dinner with nothing flashy.
items.meta: Si Sumang Road · small shop · pet-friendly

items.name: O Mookata Sisaket
items.blurb: A popular mookata that's had a Wongnai review page for a long time — a regular for people in that area. The ingredient lineup covers the standards, prices are friendly, and it's good for an easy dinner without driving far.

items.name: Sum Hua Steak & BBQ
items.blurb: A Korean BBQ spot that also does steak and spaghetti under one roof. It leans on Korean-style marinated meat in bite-sized portions, good for anyone who wants to try Korean BBQ without committing to a whole buffet — plus single-plate dishes as a backup for people who'd rather not grill.
items.meta: In Sisaket town · Korean BBQ + steak

items.name: Piyada Shabu & Mookata, Pho Branch
items.blurb: A satellite branch of Piyada on the other side of town, with the same concept: pay-by-weight, all-you-can-eat, no time limit. Handy if the main branch is packed or you're closer to this side. Budget-friendly since you only pay for what you eat.
items.meta: Pho area · pay-by-weight · no time limit

items.name: Mookata at the Town Night Market
items.blurb: If you really want to eat on a tight budget, the evening night markets in Sisaket town have pay-by-weight mookata stalls with grills set up to eat on the spot. Fast and cheap, with homemade dipping sauce — good for travelers who want a light meal before heading back to their room.
items.meta: Town evening night market · pay-by-weight · low budget

blocks.title: How to pick a spot
blocks.html: If you're coming in a big group and eat a lot, a pay-by-weight place like Piyada or Si Thong works out better — you pay for what you actually eat, with no time limit. But if you'd rather pay one flat price with no scale-watching, a per-person buffet like Nabhee or Green Garden gives you a clearer per-head budget.

blocks.text: Pay-by-weight vs per-person buffet vs BBQ sets — how to choose

blocks.html: Sisaket gives you three styles of mookata. Pay-by-weight charges for the weight of ingredients you pick up — the upside is you don't have to over-eat to get your money's worth and nothing goes to waste, so it's good for lighter eaters. Per-person buffets charge one flat price for unlimited helpings, good for groups who eat a lot and want a fixed per-head budget. Korean BBQ sets focus on quality marinated meat in right-sized portions, good for couples or small groups who'd rather have bolder flavor than all-you-can-eat volume.

items: Light eaters, small group — go pay-by-weight; you pay for actual weight and don't have to over-eat to make it worth it.
Big eaters, big group — a per-person buffet gives a clear per-head budget, unlimited helpings, better value than paying by weight.
Care about meat quality — Korean BBQ sets get you bold marinated meat in right-sized portions, nothing wasted.
Want the atmosphere — Si Thong & Camping has comfortable open-air seating, great for a long evening.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Mookata spots open mainly for dinner and prices can rise with ingredient costs. The prices listed here are rough figures from reviews — check the shop's page again before you go. At pay-by-weight places your per-person cost depends on how much you eat. Some shops have several branches and a few have moved location in the past, so pull up the latest pin on their page or call to confirm if you're coming as a big group.

faq.q: Which Sisaket mookata is the best value?
faq.a: If you don't eat much, a pay-by-weight place like Piyada Shabu & Mookata is the best value — you pay for the weight you actually eat, with no time limit. For big eaters in a group, a per-person buffet like Nabhee at around 289 baht gives a clearer per-head budget.

faq.q: What's the difference between pay-by-weight and per-person mookata?
faq.a: Pay-by-weight charges for the weight of ingredients you pick up — the upside is you don't over-eat to get your money's worth and nothing goes to waste, so it suits lighter eaters. Per-person charges one flat price for unlimited helpings, good for groups who eat a lot and want a fixed per-head budget.

Yes. Green Garden, near Sisaket Rajabhat, is a Korean-style BBQ–shabu buffet that serves pickled seafood. Sum Hua does Korean BBQ alongside steak under one roof. Both suit people who want bolder marinated meat over all-you-can-eat volume.

faq.q: What time do Sisaket mookata spots open?
faq.a: Most are dinner spots, open from late afternoon into the night, roughly 4pm–11pm. Popular buffets get packed in the early evening, so going around 5pm helps you grab a table first — and check the shop's page beforehand in case they're closed that day.

faq.q: Is there a pet-friendly mookata in Sisaket?
faq.a: Yes. Suk Lon Mookata on Si Sumang Road is a small spot that reviewers say is dog-friendly. The vibe is laid-back, good for a chill dinner when you want to bring your pet along.
